summary.en: Choose between learning with answers, finding unnamed groups, and learning through rewards.
summary.bn: উত্তর নিয়ে শেখা, নামহীন দল খোঁজা আর পুরস্কার পেয়ে শেখার মধ্যে কাজ অনুযায়ী পথ বেছে নাও।

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: Change the help, keep the cards

practice.title: Match three tasks
practice.statementHtml: Match named fruit prediction, unnamed toy grouping and reward-seeking maze moves to learning setups. Give the feedback for each.
hints: Start with what the learner is given.
practice.answerHtml: Named fruits are supervised because correct answers are supplied. Toy grouping is unsupervised because no group names are given. Maze action learning is reinforcement learning because actions lead to rewards and later opportunities.

practice.title: Same objects, new job
practice.statementHtml: Explain how six toy cards can support both supervised and unsupervised tasks.
hints: Change the question and supplied help.
practice.answerHtml: With shape labels, predicting the name of a new toy is supervised. Remove those answers and ask for useful similarity groups, and the task is unsupervised. The toys need not change.

practice.title: A delayed token
practice.statementHtml: A player takes three moves and earns a token only at the goal. Explain why the first move matters.
hints: Consider which later squares it makes reachable.
practice.answerHtml: The first move changes the state and can enable a route to the goal. Its immediate reward is not the whole story. Reinforcement learning concerns reward across a sequence, so earlier choices can matter.

practice.title: Text targets and truth
practice.statementHtml: Explain how a text model can learn without every word being hand-labelled yet still produce false claims.
hints: Separate predicting a hidden word from checking an event.
practice.answerHtml: Existing text supplies next-word or hidden-word targets during self-supervision. The learner can absorb common wording, including mistakes and fiction. Predicting a plausible continuation does not verify whether the resulting claim is true.

quiz.prompt: Read the games table. Which row supplies later rewards instead of an answer label for each example?
options: Fruit name
Maze moves
Toy groups
All three rows supply identical feedback
quiz.explanation: The maze row gives rewards after actions. Fruit names supply known answers, while the toy task supplies no group names.

caption.en: Three games offer different kinds of feedback.

quiz.prompt: The six grey toy points have no class labels. What task fits this picture?
options: Copy a supplied correct fruit name for every point
Prove that grey is the true toy category
Seek useful groups of similar toys
Learn a maze policy from rewards already displayed
quiz.explanation: The points provide observations without answer names. Grouping by visible similarity fits an unsupervised task.

caption.en: Six toy measurements without supplied class labels.
caption.bn: দলের label ছাড়া ছয় খেলনার মাপ।

quiz.prompt: A fruit table gives sizes and correct names for training. Which setup is being used?
options: Unsupervised learning because the learner is a machine
Reinforcement learning because a name is pleasant
No learning can use names
Supervised learning
quiz.explanation: Known target answers provide supervision. The technique used to build the rule does not change that feedback source.

quiz.prompt: Why does supervised learning not require a teacher beside the computer?
options: Recorded correct answers can supply the supervision
A learner can always know unseen labels without evidence
The word supervised describes a colour
Every computer must supervise itself without data
quiz.explanation: A stored labelled table gives the answer comparisons even when no person is present during training.

quiz.prompt: Predicting a numeric visitor count from earlier days with recorded outcomes is usually what setup?
options: Always reinforcement learning because the answer is numeric
Supervised learning
Always unsupervised because counts have no names
Not learning because counts are not photographs
quiz.explanation: Supervision can supply a number as the target. It is not restricted to category names.

quiz.prompt: One child groups toys by shape and another by colour. With no supplied answers, what should we ask?
options: Which child copied the hidden official labels?
Which grouping must be wrong because it differs?
Which grouping serves the intended purpose?
Which child used the larger pencil?
quiz.explanation: Different similarities can support different goals. A shelf-packing task may favour shape while an art task favours colour.

quiz.prompt: Mina adds ball/block labels and asks for a new toy name. What changed?
options: The toys physically changed into a maze
Unsupervised learning always produces perfect ball names
The labels automatically become rewards over time
The task now has known answers for supervised learning
quiz.explanation: The same objects can enter a new setup when answer labels are supplied. Classify the task, not just the objects.

quiz.prompt: What makes the maze example a reinforcement setup?
options: Moves affect later states and rewards guide action choices
Every square already has its correct fruit answer
The player only groups motionless pictures
The prize is printed but no behaviour can change
quiz.explanation: The learner acts, experiences consequences and aims for reward over time. This differs from assigning a known label to a card.

quiz.prompt: A useful early maze move earns no immediate token. Why might it still be learned?
options: Unrewarded moves can never influence learning
It can enable a later reward
The future reward must already be a fruit name
A model can ignore every consequence indefinitely
quiz.explanation: Delayed feedback matters in action sequences. The immediate token count may not describe the value of a whole route.

quiz.prompt: A shop prints a voucher after every fifth visit by a fixed rule. Is that alone reinforcement learning?
options: Yes; any voucher proves reinforcement learning
Yes; counting visits is always learned
No; rewards alone do not establish a learner adjusting actions
No; learning systems can never involve shops
quiz.explanation: The shop follows an instruction. A reinforcement claim needs learning from action consequences, not merely a reward appearing.

quiz.prompt: In self-supervised next-word training, where can the training target come from?
options: Only a human writing a fresh label for every word
A guaranteed record of the writer’s secret intentions
The colour of the computer case
The next word in existing text
quiz.explanation: Text itself can provide a target after earlier words are shown. That reduces manual labelling without making generated claims automatically true.

quiz.prompt: What should you conclude if a language model completes a sentence plausibly?
options: It produced a plausible continuation, which may still be false
The described event definitely happened
The model has checked every relevant fact
The model must feel what the writer felt
quiz.explanation: Pattern-based text prediction and factual verification are different. A fluent completion does not establish the event it describes.

keyPoints.en: Known example answers support supervised learning.
keyPoints.bn: জানা উত্তর থাকলে supervised শেখা হয়।

keyPoints.en: Finding structure without answer labels is unsupervised learning.
keyPoints.bn: উত্তরের label ছাড়া ধরন খোঁজা unsupervised।

keyPoints.en: Actions and later rewards guide reinforcement learning.
keyPoints.bn: কাজ আর পরের পুরস্কার reinforcement শেখায়।

keyPoints.en: The same objects can support several learning tasks.
keyPoints.bn: একই বস্তুতে শেখার কাজ আলাদা হতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: A useful grouping depends on its purpose.
keyPoints.bn: দল কাজে লাগে কি না, উদ্দেশ্য দেখে বলো।

keyPoints.en: Self-supervised text training draws targets from text itself.
keyPoints.bn: Self-supervised লেখায় লেখা থেকেই target আসে।

keyPoints.en: A plausible continuation can still describe something false.

examQuestions.question: Compare supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning using the help supplied.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Supervised learning receives example answers and learns to predict them on new inputs. Unsupervised learning seeks structure without supplied labels. Reinforcement learning chooses actions whose consequences and rewards shape future behaviour.

examQuestions.question: Six fruit cards have labels. Four labels are revealed for practice and two are hidden for prediction. How many labelled practice examples can the learner use?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Only four labelled examples are available for learning in this activity. The two covered labels remain checking answers until predictions are recorded. The physical presence of six cards does not reveal six training answers.

examQuestions.question: Design two sensible unnamed groupings for two red balls, two blue balls and two red blocks.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A shape grouping places the four balls together and the two blocks together. A colour grouping places four red toys together and two blue toys together. State whether packing by shape or arranging colours is the goal before judging usefulness.

examQuestions.question: Explain self-supervised language-model training to a younger learner without claiming it reads minds.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Show a sentence with its next word covered. Earlier words become clues and the covered word becomes an answer drawn from the text. Repeating that task teaches patterns. Later completions can sound natural while being factually wrong or unlike a particular writer’s intention.
